title: Variables and Assignment
content:
What problem does this solve?
Programs need to remember values — a character's name, current health, or score — and reuse them later.

Basic syntax
  name = expression

What actually happens
The right-hand side is evaluated first. Then Python attaches that resulting object to the name on the left. A variable is a label pointing at a value, not a fixed box that permanently owns one type.

Practical example: a character sheet uses names like health and level so later code can update them without rewriting every print statement.
concepts: Assignment evaluates the right side, then binds the name on the left
Variable names should describe meaning (health, not x)
Reassigning a name makes it point at a new value

examples.title: Create and use variables
examples.explanation: name refers to the string object "Aria". health refers to the integer 100.

examples.title: Reassignment
examples.explanation: gold + 10 creates 60, then gold is rebound to 60. The old 50 may be discarded.

common_mistakes: Writing health == 100 when you meant to assign ( == compares )
Using a variable before assigning it — that raises NameError

exercises.title: Character summary variables
exercises.prompt:
Create variables:
  name  -> the string "Rook"
  health -> the integer 80
  level  -> the integer 3

Then print each on its own line in that order (name, health, level).
exercises.starter_code: # Create name, health, and level, then print them
hints: Strings need quotes; integers do not.
Assign all three names first, then call print three times.

Example shape:
name = "Rook"
health = 80
level = 3
print(name)
print(health)
print(level)

exercises.title: Finish the assignment
exercises.prompt: Complete the code so attack equals strength plus the weapon bonus. Replace the placeholder value.
exercises.starter_code:
strength = 12
weapon_bonus = 3
attack = None  # TODO: set this to strength + weapon_bonus
print(attack)
hints: Replace None with an expression using the two variables.
Use the + operator to add integers.
